sections.h2: What makes selling a house in Greenburgh different from other Westchester towns?
sections.html:
Greenburgh is a large town with six villages and a sizeable unincorporated area, so the rules that apply to your house depend on which part of it you live in. The town sits in western Westchester County, with the Hudson River as its western edge, Yonkers to the south, Mount Pleasant to the north, and White Plains and Scarsdale to the east.

Wikipedia's entry on Greenburgh says the town was founded in 1788, covers about 36 square miles of which 30 are land, and had 95,397 residents in the 2020 census. Roughly half of those residents live inside the villages. The rest live in unincorporated areas that include the Fairview, Greenville and Hartsdale census-designated places, along with neighborhoods such as North Elmsford and South Ardsley.

That split matters at sale time. The town Building Department says it handles complaints only for the unincorporated part of Greenburgh, not the villages, and the Tax Department tells village residents to contact their own Village Hall for due dates. A seller in Tarrytown or Dobbs Ferry therefore has to check two sets of offices.

sections.h2: How expensive is the typical Greenburgh house?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's profile reports a median owner-occupied value of $697,100 for 2020 to 2024, which puts many Greenburgh sales in the range where closing costs and the state mansion tax threshold come into play. The numbers below come from that profile.

The 34-minute average commute fits a town whose Metro-North stations on the Hudson and Harlem lines draw buyers who work in the city. Median gross rent is $2,316 a month, a useful comparison if you are weighing a sale against renting the house out.

sections.h2: What transport and schools shape a Greenburgh sale?
sections.html:
• Rail: the Hudson Line has stops at Hastings-on-Hudson, Dobbs Ferry, Ardsley-on-Hudson, Irvington and Tarrytown, and the Harlem Line stops at Hartsdale.
  • Roads: the New York State Thruway (I-87), the Cross Westchester Expressway, the Saw Mill River, Bronx River and Sprain Brook parkways, US 9, NY-9A, NY-100 and NY-119 all cross the town.
  • Buses: the county's Bee-Line system serves the town.
  • School districts: the town tax office collects bills for 10 school districts, so the district named on your tax bill is the one a buyer will ask about first.

Because the school district changes the tax bill so sharply from one street to the next, ask for the latest bill before you price the house.

sections.h2: Which Greenburgh building rules affect a sale?
sections.html:
A permit is required for any construction, repair, improvement, modification or demolition, according to the Building Department FAQ. Roofing counts: a one or two family roof replacement needs a permit with drawings, and structural changes need plans stamped by a New York State architect or engineer.

  • Every size of shed needs a permit. Only one shed per lot is allowed, it must sit in the rear yard, and it cannot exceed 150 square feet or 10 feet in height.
  • Fences need no building permit if they stay at or under six feet in a front or side yard and eight feet in a rear yard, but corner lots have a 30 inch limit near the corner.
  • Repaving an existing driveway needs no permit. Enlarging it does, and a curb cut or right-of-way permit may also be required from Public Works.
  • Removing or abandoning a heating oil tank requires its own permit and inspection.
  • Short-term rentals are not listed as a permitted use in any residential zoning district.

The last point matters if a buyer wants to run the house as a vacation rental. The department's forms page says applications are taken in person or by mail on weekdays at 177 Hillside Avenue, so check the posted hours before you go.

sections.h2: How do Greenburgh property taxes work at closing?
sections.html:
The Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes collects more than a quarter billion dollars a year for the county, the town, fire districts and the ten school districts, which the Tax Department page calls the largest municipal collection agency in Westchester. The first part of the 2026 school tax was due September 30, 2026, and that date has passed. Ask the tax office for the next deadline, and for a payoff figure before the closing.

  • Checks go to the Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes at 177 Hillside Avenue. Online payment is handled through the town's municipal tax payment site, with ACH payments free of fees.
  • Liens cannot be paid online and must be settled with the Tax Office.
  • The office stays open until 7 p.m. on the last collection days, January 31, April 30 and September 30.
  • New owners should contact the tax office so bills reach them and not the previous owner.

The page also repeats two state rules. A bill that never arrives does not cancel the tax or the interest (Real Property Tax Law section 922), and the Receiver has no power to waive penalties (section 920). A seller who has moved out should update the mailing address in writing with the tax office.

sections.h2: How does Greenburgh set assessments and handle disputes?
sections.html:
The town's Assessment Rolls page explains that the tentative roll is public by June 1 and the Board of Assessment Review rules on appeals before the roll becomes final on September 15. The final rolls are a snapshot as of that date, and later small claims changes do not appear in them. The current roll listed on the page is the 2026 Final Assessment Roll.

If your assessment looks high against recent sales on your street, review the roll before you accept an offer, since a buyer will see the same record. Questions about the latest assessment go to the Assessor's Office.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed in Westchester involve?
sections.html:
Deeds for Greenburgh houses are recorded with the Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division. The clerk's deed guide says a deed must come with a cover page created in the PREP system, the state TP-584 form, the RP-5217 transfer report, and a payment cover page with fees and tax.

State transfer tax is $2 for each $500 of consideration, rounded up to the next $500. The clerk's own example is a $404,501 price rounded to $405,000, which produces $1,620 of tax. At the $697,100 median value the tax would be about $2,790. A separate mansion tax of one percent applies to a one, two or three family house or condo conveyed for $1,000,000 or more, which some Greenburgh and village sales will reach.

The clerk does not prepare deeds or give advice on them, so use your closing attorney for the document itself.

sections.h2: What should a Greenburgh seller prepare first?
sections.html:
• The property condition disclosure statement under Real Property Law section 462, signed and given to the buyer before a binding contract.
  • Open permits and any certificate of occupancy or completion for finished space.
  • Your latest town, county and school tax bills, and village bills if you live in a village.
  • A payoff letter from the lender, plus any lien paperwork.
  • A plan for the STAR credit: the state asks owners to close a registration after a sale.

faqs.q: Does the Greenburgh Building Department cover villages like Tarrytown or Irvington?
faqs.a: No. The department says it handles complaints in the unincorporated town, not the villages. Village homes follow the village's own building and tax offices.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace my roof in Greenburgh?
faqs.a: Yes. A one or two family roof covering replacement needs a building permit with drawings, and structural roof changes need plans from a licensed architect or engineer.

faqs.q: Can a buyer use a Greenburgh house for short-term rentals?
faqs.a: Not under the zoning rules the town describes. Short-term rentals are not a permitted use in any residential zoning district, so a buyer planning that use should ask the Building Department before closing.

faqs.q: How much is the New York State transfer tax on a Greenburgh sale?
faqs.a: It is $2 for every $500 of price, rounded up to the next $500. A sale at $700,000 would carry $2,800. Sales at $1,000,000 or more of one to three family homes also owe a one percent mansion tax.

The Greenburgh Receiver of Taxes at 177 Hillside Avenue collects county, town, fire district and school taxes for the town's 10 school districts. Village residents get separate due dates from their Village Hall.
